description:
`==` means two different things depending on where it is written.

  fnp same?(a, b) when a == b, do: :equal
  fnp same?(_a, _b), do: :different

  same?(1, 1.0)   fz both doors: :different     Elixir: :equal
  1 == 1.0        fz both doors: true           Elixir: true

The same token widens in an expression and is strict in a guard. Pre-existing --
it reproduces at 67e09d373, where interp_value_eq already had
(Int, Float) => false -- but it was invisible until `==` started widening in
expressions, because before that both were strict and merely wrong together.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN fz-5xp.22: native guards lower to
Prim::BinOp(IrBinOp::Eq) (jobs/native.rs, lower_guard_binop), and PATTERN
MATCHING emits the same prim from many sites -- Region::Equal, AssertLiteral,
map-miss checks, list tests. Matching must stay strict (`1.0` never matches a
literal `1`), so the two cannot both be served by one IR op. Widening only the
interpreter's guard path was tried and reverted: it would have traded a
consistent-but-wrong answer for a NEW three-door divergence, which is worse.

WHAT THE FIX LOOKS LIKE: the IR needs to distinguish the `==` OPERATOR from
structural identity, the way the source now does since fz-5xp.22 added `===`.
Either a second IrBinOp variant, or guards emitting the fz_op_eq extern rather
than Prim::BinOp. Then guards widen, matching stays strict, and
lower_eq_binop's `widen_numerics` parameter -- which currently infers from the
call site what the source should have said -- can be deleted.

RELIED-ON BY NOTHING NOW: the runtime library used to depend on this accident.
`List.member?` and `delete_first` were written `when head == value` and got
identity semantics only because guards happen to be strict, which matched
Elixir (whose member?/2 and -- use `===`) by coincidence rather than by
intent. fz-5xp.22 rewrote them to say `===` explicitly, so fixing the guard
will not change their behaviour.

GATE: behavior/equality_widening_and_identity.fz covers the expression side.
A guard case belongs there once this is fixed.
title: `==` is strict in a guard and widening in an expression
